item.title: Abiogenesis (SCP): Forum Criticism Team - Junior Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Duccy boi, per the Site's Criticism Policy found here: http://www.scp-wiki.net/criticism-policy

Forum critique should be relatively in-depth.

Try to make sure you give enough criticism that an author can tell the quality of their entire concept/draft. What do you find cool about it? What about it is original? What would the K class scenarios constitute to this? Could you expand more on why you think the plot could be tightened by meeting somebody like another time traveler? Please try to endeavour in writing a more detailed analysis when dropping critique in the future, as it would be of a better benefit to the author.

If you need more assistance with how to properly write a review, please consider referring to this thread for guidance: http://www.scpwiki.com/forum/t-9804362/so-you-want-to-be-a-concept-reviewer

Sputnik One, since this thread has been disrupted, please consider referring to this thread if you are in need of a reviewer:
http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-13282692/how-to-get-more-reviews

item.title: A Simple Pub (looking for Feedback and Greenlight): Re: A Simple Pub (looking for Feedback and Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
The bartender and owner is relatively open and talkative about the people he's met and places he's been, but when the foundation start trying to find out

some of the more personal questions about his and the bars history he starts getting more dismissive and less talkative. Multiple odd things found in the bar hint to some
sort of hidden past of the place.
This is very vague. You get 400 words total to explain a concept. Take those extra words you haven't used and explain.

So I would suggest that you work in some actual narrative here. What is the reason you're interested in this bar proprietor? What is the character like? Why should the reader care? Is the an arc? How does the Foundation discover and what do they want to do with it?

item.title: Zombies with cool things for hands (Seeking Greenlight): Re: Zombies with cool things for hands (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Made a reply, and then noticed you had edited your answer :D

Anyways, main plotline is the MTF team through the city, fighting the zombies. As they progress (about 75% in through the story), they find the kid who is crying and apologizing profusely. He tells them he just wanted something fun to happen, that everything in the town was dumb and boring, every day was just the same.

The kid is escorted to the end by the team, to show them where his house is, and the notebook. The final fight ensues, with The Final Countdown playing in the background from a zombie standing nearby with a boombox held high.

The MTF calls in helicopters to help deal with it, explosions, rock music and gunfire. As it dies, a few other kids run out from where they had been hiding while the MTF goes down in the basement to disrupt the ritual the kid started, ending the phenomena. The kids are standing in the street shouting in excitement about how awesome it was, applauding the boy who started it.

As the MTF call in help to have the mess cleaned up they hear some of the kids shouting about how it was so awesome that they should do it every week.

item.title: Return to Monke - Greenlight Request/Review: Return to Monke - Greenlight Request/Review
item.content:encoded:
Hello, this will be my first SCP idea/greenlight, and I'm hoping this makes as much sense to the general public as it does to me.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article (SCP-5284 preferred, not picky on numbers otherwise)
Elevator Pitch
An iceberg floating just 50 knots North of Antarctica is beholden to many phenomena. For one, the glacier itself seems to react to the shortcomings of mankind, almost being frustrated at the existence of the human race. What exactly is below the surface, and who was responsible for this odd mesh of science and nature?

Central Narrative: The main SCP item is the glacier, and SCP-XXXX-2A is found within the glacier. This is an anomalous gas similar to the C-terminus debacle in SCP-3966 (with the "missing" valence electrons of the oxygen inside SCP-XXXX-2A being monkey paws). When inhaled by a human, they slowly but surely turn into a monkey (hereby SCP-XXXX-2B)

SCP-XXXX-3 are a series of thirteen shrines/steles with an unknown cognitohazardous language. While English operates on a series of words conveying concepts, this language does the exact opposite; communicating in conviction, feeling, empathy.

Over the course of the article, a journal is found from a monkey who was bestowed intelligence by the Avatar of the Earth. Our monkey scientist then grapples with the stupidity of mankind, before realizing that the only way to protect what gave him the ground to stand on, is to pack everything away and create a failsafe, so that Earth may live on.

End of the article implies that the iceberg is melting faster from this point onwards.

Relies on themes of: Intelligence, nature, and whether the nature of humankind is to create or destroy. Cliché, I know.

Hook/Attention Grabber: Trying to lure readers in with the absurdity of "haha what if the return to monkey meme was real", but trying to take it in a darker more serious sense.

Additional Notes: I've had this idea swimming around in my head for months, and it was either this or writing a Pataphysics skip. Heavily inspired by Silent Spring and my own experiences in the outdoors as an Eagle Scout.

If you made it this far, thank you and I hope you have a wonderful day!

item.title: Zombies with cool things for hands (Seeking Greenlight): Re: Zombies with cool things for hands (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Thanks Scorpion! I've actually got quite a few jokes lying around for the concept before I penned it out as an idea.

The conproc and descriptions are both going to be fairly short, to get the story started a bit quickly. The discovery of the SCP is the Foundation noticing a television broadcast from a VERY small local TV station, a kid from the school newspaper is interviewing a glam rock band from the town. They're talking about making it big, their latest album selling a whopping 1200 records, behaving like they're being interviewed by Rolling Stones Magazine. They used to be so poor that they couldn't afford both groupies and roadies, they had to combine the two, find women of a certain size that allowed them to also chug heavy music equipment, women the band affectionally nicknamed Groadies. Then the zombies break through the back wall, revealing it to be cheap cardboard with a white sheet covering it.

From then we move to the MTF team that has to make it through the town, get to the house where the ritual circle is in the basement. Basically the story is the MTF team making it through town, with lots of little fun jokes coming from the zombie concept along the way. They haven't found out about the source of the phenomena, so they're obviously perplexed.

Some of the fun stuff I thought up for the concept, as they progress:

They come across a zombie that has kitchen mixers for hands, it's alone, scavenging in the street. One of the soldiers quietly mocks it, about how useless it is compared to the others. Just then, the building next to them explodes and the street is covered in dust and debris, a zombie with a blackpowder cannon for hands had been hiding on a nearby roof. The soldiers hear pained screaming, and run to help, finding the kitchen mixer zombie and the soldier who mocked it, the kitchen mixers having completely been entangled with his hair as he's dragged down the street by the zombie.

They see a ferocious pack of howling zombies running down a intersecting street, and after several moments pass, they see a single zombie coming down the same street, slowly dragging two heavy anvils it has instead of hands. It drags them slowly… slowly… slowly across the street, trying to catch up. Just as it almost makes it across, the howling pack comes back the other way, runs around the anvil zombie and off the other side. The anvil zombie bows its head defeatedly before turning around to follow the pack, slowly dragging the anvils along.

item.title: Last Flight Out (SEEKING GREENLIGHT): Last Flight Out (SEEKING GREENLIGHT)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article (Aiming for SCP-5127)

Elevator Pitch

  • Anomalous airplane
  • Appears at airports that are either closed, either for the night or due to bad weather
  • It's destination is always one in high demand at the current aiport
  • Up to 26 passengers can 'transfer' to this flight
  • Plane does not show up on radar, and does not recieve instruction from air traffic control
  • Flight always lasts 2 hours, 47 minutes from take off to landing
  • Will land in some forsaken place, such as in the middle of Siberia, the Sahara, or even in the ocean
  • Aiport it lands at is also anomalous, appearing from the inside to be an exact copy of whatever aiport the plane was supposed to land at
  • Airport will spontaneously generate about 30 minutes before the plane lands
  • Aiport will remain in existince for exactly 75 minutes, before both it and the airplane disappear

Central Narrative: Honestly I don't really understand what this part is supposed to mean, so for the the time being, I will say None. But please feel free to give me advice on what to put here, as well as how to expand and improve this SCP.

item.title: 'Baby-Aid' - Seeking feedback and Greenlight: 'Baby-Aid' - Seeking feedback and Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: Let's make conception convenient! Just put in a drop of that prime stock D-N-A and receive a child in under an hour! Perfect for the busy mommies and hard working daddies! The children even come out with little improvements, a gift from our home to yours!

Central Narrative: The Foundation recovers numerous instances of the same anomalous appliance from the 1950s found within an old storage unit. Thought to be an unsuccessful product that never went into circulation, the Foundation begins testing the devices different settings using Class-D personnel. They produce children on every setting the machine has, finding each to be differently cybernetic but otherwise non anomalous. They designate the SCP safe and put it under secure storage at a low security site and debate what to do with the children; while some more paranoid and morally conscious staff members initially recommend euthanasia, the children are healthy despite their implants and found to develop normally. The children are then placed in Foundation care until they can be neutralised if further anomalies develop from them or they can be integrated into the Foundation.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Initially just an anomalous item, the children produced raise the question of what the Foundation does with the innocent in the aftermath of the anomalous. While the more cynical among us would expect the worst, the Foundation has proven to be surprising and the situation proves both their compassion and their pragmatism.

Additional Notes: I like the idea of a small story and otherwise basic SCP being the catalyst for one of the Foundation's more compassionate moments in history. Sometime I feel they're pushed beyond morally grey pragmatists into villainous territory and think they have the capacity to be kind, even if it's tinged with clinical coldness and only just once in a while.

item.title: Zombies with cool things for hands (Seeking Greenlight): Re: Zombies with cool things for hands (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
This isn't a joke SCP. This is mainlister material, provided you write it well.

The most dangerous things the Foundation faces are never the doomsday cults or horrifying monsters- it's the ones involving phrases like "Amateur Thaumaturge" and "unattended 9-year-old".

All you have to do is take everything you're thinking of, and pit it against an elite team of agents questioning the life decisions that have them under siege by badly drawn ninja dinosaurs and squirrels driving monster trucks.

Only thing really holding me back from an immediate greenlight is that I'd like to see a little more fleshing out of the plot. Don't need extreme detail or a full blown outline; just sell me on the idea that you have some sort of coherent plotline figured out between the notebook coming to life and the showdown with the Pikazilla OC. (For instance, where are the townsfolk in all of this, not to mention the kid and his dad?)

Bonus points if you manage to have this end in some heartwarming moment without jumping the shark.

item.title: Wooden Nickels -Idea for Greenlight: Wooden Nickels -Idea for Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Standard layout + Addenda

Elevator Pitch:
SCP-XXXX is a life-size wax replica of George Washington. Physically all looks normal excluding it's face, which has been disfigured, leaving only a pair of the president's famous wooden teeth visible. Object will actively roam and attempt to locate wood of any form. If the object senses wood within about a 10 meter radius (through unknown means), object will enter a frenzied state and produce a knife from within it's wax body, designated as SCP-XXXX-1. In the state, entity will attempt to dismantle any wooden matter in the area and begin whittling it down into "wooden nickels". SCP-XXXX-1 is unnaturally efficient at carving wood, with object able to manufacture a coin about every 8 seconds. These coins, designated as SCP-XXXX-2, will upon physical human contact transfigure into a real coin. The coins will maintain this form for 78 hours after initial contact. The type of coin seems to be linked to the type of wood used (research ongoing). Researchers have also observed that entity will also instinctively pick at leaves, which upon human contact will briefly transfigure into the shape of paper currency before melting into pulp.

Central Narrative:
A central focus is the implication that this anomalous object was likely artificially created through unknown means for the express purpose of producing counterfeit currency. Researchers speculate though that object is likely an unsuccessful prototype, evident by a number of "flaws" that would make a counterfeit operation difficult to achieve at scale. This leaves it open for the possibility of other similar objects having been made. Article will also detail the acquisition of the object and the discovery of a violent reaction the object has when it becomes conscious that it possesses wood on it's body (the disfigurement of it's face was a result of attempts to remove them).

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
I plan to attach a photo of the entity that will hopefully hook the reader into learning more and will draw them in further with the idea that this object was made for a criminal purpose by and unknown creator.

Additional Notes: N/A

item.title: Zombies with cool things for hands (Seeking Greenlight): Zombies with cool things for hands (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Joke SCP

Elevator Pitch: A small town, a dad who's the leader of an amateur thaumaturgical cult, and his 9-year old kid with a notebook titled "Really cool stuff". One fateful day, the young kid sneaks into his dads basement and places his notebook at the center of the ritual setup, unleashing everything within it.

Central Narrative: Follow a team of daring MTF soldiers as they have to fight their way through a city occupied by zombies that all have cool things instead of hands! What do you mean by cool things, you might say? Oh lord, anything! Axes? Yup! Swords? Yup! AK-47s? Of course. Lightsabers, blackpowder cannons, katanas, grenade launchers, nunchucks and chainsaws. If you're lucky you might even run into the zombie with a boombox for hands, that plays only The Final Countdown by Europe, and the volume is set to eleven!

If the brave MTF team make it to the boys house, they have to fight the ultimate enemy. The completely original creation of his called Pikazilla, a 50 ft. tall version of Pikachu that shoots lightning and eats geography teachers.

So greenlight this SCP today and experience the best hard-hitting and uncompromising ACTION of the 80s!

item.title: The Hinterland Division (How many apocalypses could there be?): Re: The Hinterland Division (How many apocalypses could there be?)
item.content:encoded: I think that he discovers the existence and history of the position that i already mentioned he is moved up to, which leads him to know as much about the Foundation as the O5 council themselves, within this information he finds out that the entirety of the Hinterland Division that he sacrificed so much for was based upon lies, namely lies about the actual existence of several of the world threat entities that he was working to stop, which were made up from the beginning, the explanation behind this being to "Convince him that he is capable of stopping them with fakes, throw in some carnage, tactically get rid of expendables, come up with any backstories you need, we need him to think that he is a capable leader saving the world. Once that's done he'll be psychologically ready to handle the real Hinterland Division." after this he discovered that there are actual world threats that he is expected to deal with. The ones that he had already beaten, needing to sacrifice countless lives and abandon his morals to do so, having been a test run, threats designed by the Foundation to challenge his abilities and turn him into the candidate required, the problem is that all of the things that he did to deal with those threats was real, and the O5 had let him continue, knowing that if they stepped in it would ruin the plan. So basically he discovers that the Foundation willingly allowed hundreds of personnel and innocents, even children to be hurt, tortured, and killed in order to save humanity. What scared him was not that the foundation did this, he knew they would do anything to protect humanity, he was scared because he realized the plan worked, and he himself had changed and no longer cared about those peoples lives, and was now ready to sacrifice everything to the Foundation.
